title: Joel And I — EN/HI/SW/MI/YO — Chas Lessons #3 (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar Hindi Swahili Maori Yoruba language learning dry wit deadpan 104bpm upright bass brushed snare multilingual grammar lesson Ubuntu collectivist warm
lyrics:
[Verse 1 - English]
Swan River. One sentence. Permanent.
"Oh — you mean Joel and I."
Collectivist cultures already know this rule.
Ubuntu: I am because we are.

[Verse 2 - Hindi, with English translations]
जोएल और मैं (Joel and I)
मैं — हमेशा अंत में जाता है (I — always goes last)
दूसरा नाम हटाओ, पढ़ो जो बचा है (Remove the other name, read what remains)
"मैं पानी की तरफ जा रहा हूँ" — सही (I am going to the water — correct)
तो यह है जोएल और मैं (So it's Joel and I)
तुम्हारे शब्दों का क्रम (The order of your words)
तुम्हारी प्राथमिकताओं का क्रम है (Is the order of your priorities)

[Chorus - Swahili, with English translations]
Joel na mimi (Joel and I)
Mimi daima inakwenda mwisho (I always goes last)
Ondoa jina lingine, soma kilichobaki (Remove the other name, read what's left)
"Ninaenda kwa maji" — sahihi (I am going to the water — correct)
Kwa hivyo ni Joel na mimi (So it's Joel and I)
Lugha ni tabia mapema (Language is character in advance)
Ubuntu: Mimi ni kwa sababu sisi ni (Ubuntu: I am because we are)

[Bridge - Māori + Yoruba]
Māori: Ko Joel rāua ko au — ingoa tērā kei mua (Ko Joel rāua ko au — the other name goes first)
(Joel and I — name the other first)
Yoruba: Joel àti èmi — èmi kọjú (Joel and I — I goes last)
(Collectivist default — the group before the self)

[Outro - all]
English: Joel and I — one sentence — permanent
Hindi: जोएल और मैं — एक वाक्य — स्थायी (Joel and I — one sentence — permanent)
Swahili: Joel na mimi — sentensi moja — ya kudumu (Joel and I — one sentence — permanent)
Māori: Ko Joel rāua ko au — tūāpō — tonu (Joel and I — night — always)
Yoruba: Joel àti èmi — gbolohùn kan — títí láé (Joel and I — one sentence — forever)
